knowledge_point.title: Determining the Lengths of the Major and Minor Axes Given the Equation of an Ellipse

question.:question/problem:
What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of an ellipse with equation 
$\frac{{x}^{2}}{100}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{55}=1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

In the given equation, we have ${a}^{2}=100$ and ${b}^{2}=55.$

- Since ${a}^{2}=100,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{100}=10.$

- Since ${b}^{2}=55,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{55}.$

So the semi-major axis has length $a=10,$ and the semi-minor axis has length $b=\sqrt{55}.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2a=2\cdot 10=20,$ and the minor axis has length $2b=2\cdot \sqrt{55}=2\sqrt{55}.$
